goal: Teach one-at-a-time sensitivity reasoning: a plausible input range gives a defensible deterministic output range, distinct from numerical approximation error and model limitation.

sample_generation_method.input_context_preparation: parent inspected local strict MATLAB references with view_image; approved sample supplied as style reference
sample_generation_method.handoff_rule: Use the built-in image_gen tool in generate/reference mode only; return a blocker if unavailable.

deck_context.source_summary: For ideal Hooke's law x=F/k, hold F=10 N fixed and treat stiffness k=95-105 N/m as a plausible uncertainty around the 100 N/m baseline. Evaluate lower, baseline and upper values, report the output range, validate the baseline and distinguish parameter uncertainty from numerical approximation error and model limitation.
deck_context.locked_values: k=[95,100,105] N/m gives x=[0.10526,0.10000,0.09524] m. Force Working-exposure sweep F=[9.8,10.0,10.2] N at k=100 N/m gives x=[0.098,0.100,0.102] m. Supplied first-order independent result is 5.39%, ux≈0.00539 m for uF=0.2 N and uk=5 N/m.
deck_context.universal_constraints: Use title-only top band and a thin straight divider. Do not render headers, slide numbers, page footers, borders, logos, timings, production metadata, or unapproved numerical claims.

Hold force, equation, units and assumptions fixed

slides.title: What Range Does the Model Predict?
slides.local_context: Approved sample. Controlled parameter cases, not random trials.

slides.title: Report the Result Without False Precision
slides.intent: Turn values into a defensible physical statement.
key_points: 0.10000 m alone hides the input range
State the load, stiffness range and output range
Extra decimal places do not reduce uncertainty

layout.composition: weak report versus defensible range-based report

visual_elements.main_visual: two text cards with clear contrast

slides.local_context: Practical statement: 10 N and k 95-105 N/m give about 0.095 to 0.105 m in the ideal model.

slides.title: Core Validation: Check the Baseline
slides.intent: Use independent calculation, units and trend.
slides.local_context: A smooth graph alone is not validation.

slides.title: Three Different Reasons a Prediction Can Be Imperfect
key_points: Numerical approximation error: finite timestep, grid or iteration
Model limitation: assumptions do not fully represent reality
slides.local_context: The direct Hooke calculation here has no meaningful timestep, grid or iteration approximation error.

slides.title: Working Exposure: Compare a Second Uncertain Input
slides.intent: Change force while holding stiffness fixed.
key_points: Hold k = 100 N/m; vary F = 9.8-10.2 N
Stiffness gives the larger effect for these supplied ranges

layout.composition: large cohesive redraw of two-bar output-span comparison

required_images.fidelity: preserve bar heights 0.004 m Force and 0.010025 m Stiffness, axis Full extension span (m), categories and relative magnitudes in a full-slide redraw

constraints: State clearly that the comparison is only for the supplied input ranges.
slides.local_context: Student modification: predict and calculate force variation; do not claim stiffness is universally more important.
